message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | Atmospheric dread, iconic imagery, and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** (John Carpenter) | A tense, claustrophobic alien invasion with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** (Jonathan Demme) | A psychological thriller that blends horror with crime‑procedural intrigue. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** (Daniel Myrick & Eduardo Sánchez) | Pioneered the found‑footage style and created a new wave of horror. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (Danny Boyle) | A fast‑paced, post‑apocalyptic zombie film that redefined the genre. |
| 2004 | **Saw** (James Wan) | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that sparked a long‑running franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** (Oren Peli) | Low‑budget found‑footage film that made a huge cultural impact. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (James Wan) | A modern supernatural horror that blends folklore with a strong narrative. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (Dennis Dugan & Joss Whedon) | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and genuinely scary. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** (David Robert Mitchell) | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** (Robert Eggers) | A slow‑burn, period‑accurate horror that builds dread through atmosphere. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that mixes satire with genuine scares. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (John Krasinski) | Tension built around silence, with a strong family dynamic. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that subverts expectations with its unsettling folk‑ritual vibe. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (Leigh Whannell) | A modern retelling of the classic with a strong feminist angle. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (Nia DaCosta) | A contemporary take on a horror legend, blending social commentary with chills. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller that balances creepy atmosphere with a compelling story. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (David Freyer) | A horror‑comedy about a murderous AI doll that’s both funny and frightening. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or found‑footage—and enjoy the chills!
